title: Louis Prima at Graff's; demonstrating mallet on cymbal
summary: Sal recounts playing with Prima and shows how to play cymbal with a mallet.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: What was it that Lowe used to say, Lowe Pramee, you said, play it pretty for the people?

Well, Lowe said that. One time I was for Graff, you know what? That's what I left. My Lowe, my Lowe, my Lowe, my Lowe Pramee, with a big shot. He came with Graff. And the manager up there, you know Richard Perez. He knows I play him. He says, he's a scientist. He came on, come grab me. He said, that. He said, Leon Pramee was up there. So I went up there. I said, from the back, you know. I know Lowe, I said, man, big splash. I said, man, big splash. Overcoat, man. About dreaming all overcoat, you know, in the gaps, you know. With Kiela Schmidt, you know. So I told him, I said, I said, Lord. I told him, I said, come on, sit here, man. This is going to be. He said, come on, sit here, man. Give me some rhythm, man. Give me some rhythm. Give me some rhythm. Because we're playing a cast. I love three piece bass. Come on, man.

I told the driver, get that quick. All the girls, you know, when they're coming out, man. Da da da. Come on. Read that, man. See, we read them, Sam. I guess what the mallet meant. What the mallet meant. Yeah. Nowadays, they used to stick them one side. It's the mallet on the cymbal. Yeah. One side of the mallet, you know. Like that, see.
Very familiar with my graduation at the West End Rule.

Like that, see. Make it ring, like see. With your hand like that. That's it. Solid, man. Solid, man. On the cymbal. Choking, huh? Choking, see. Good singing, simple, see. So, I see. Play it, man. It's a rhythm, man.
